identity.name: Republic of the Rif
alt_names: Confederal Republic of the Tribes of the Rif

land.text: the Rif of the Spanish protectorate, where the Rifians captured over 130 Spanish military posts and proclaimed the Republic of the Rif in September 1921

predecessors.note: The Spanish protectorate in Morocco (Spanish Morocco) is a region of Cliopatria's Kingdom of Spain only at the edges; the Rif shape does not overlap it in 1922 or 1924.

land.text: the Rif, conquered by Spanish and French forces; the infobox names the Spanish protectorate in Morocco as successor

successors.note: Abd el-Krim surrendered on 26 or 27 May 1926; French forces also took part in the conquest.

capitals.name: Ajdir (Axdir)
capitals.note: Infobox capital Ajdir (also spelled Axdir); the page names no later seat.

rulers.name: Abd el-Krim
rulers.title: emir, then head of state
rulers.note: Named emir on 18 September 1921; The republic was formally constituted in 1923, with Abd el-Krim as head of state and Ben Hajj Hatmi as prime minister; surrendered 26-27 May 1926, deported to Reunion until 1947.

correction.text: the 1922 shape, valid from the proclamation of 18 September 1921

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1921 (18 September to December): Cliopatria's row starts in 1922, but A national gathering on 18 September 1921 agreed on Rif independence. The 1922 outline holds for 1921; the page gives no area.
4,928 km2 (20 cells, 4.5W to 2.65W, 34.9N to 35.2N) for 1922-1923; the page gives no area. The republic was formally constituted in 1923.

9,674 km2 (36 cells), +19 cells to the west (5.7W to 3.7W) over 1923: the zone Spain evacuated after Primo de Rivera visited Ben Taieb in late July 1924 and changed the withdrawal plans, pulling back from Chefchaouen and Oued Laou to the 'Primo Line' (Rif War page; no day given). Kept for 1924-1925; the shape does not contain the French-zone ground the Rifians fought over in 1925 ('advanced south into French Morocco, defeating French forces') and the Alhucemas coast (Spanish landing September 1925).

minus.text: Alhucemas Bay and Ajdir, the Rif coast and capital (secured by the Spanish fleet and army in September 1925)

correction.text: the 1924 shape without Alhucemas Bay and Ajdir, taken by Spain in September 1925

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1926 (January to 27 May): Cliopatria's row ends in 1925. The Spanish fleet and army secured Alhucemas Bay in September 1925 and a Franco-Spanish force of 200,000 to 500,000 men (the page gives both) advanced; the page does not say how much land the republic still held, so the shape is the 1924 outline without the bay (confidence 1 beyond that).

region.text: the Rif around Ajdir, Annual and the Spanish posts the Rifians took

ledger.note: 1921: the Rifians proclaim the Republic of the Rif on 18 September. A national gathering on 18 September 1921 agreed on Rif independence, named Abd el-Krim emir; the Rifians had captured over 130 Spanish military posts after Annual (1 July 1921). The page names the Rif, not a boundary.

region.text: the front with the Spanish zone, 1921-1926

ledger.note: 1921: the Rif War front with Spanish Morocco. The war ran 'from 1921 to 1926'; Abd el-Krim's Rifians defeated a Spanish offensive at Annual (collapse on 1 July 1921). The front lines are not given, so the zone is a band along the frontier of the Spanish zone.
1923: the republic is formally constituted. The republic was formally constituted in 1923, with Abd el-Krim as head of state and Ben Hajj Hatmi as prime minister.

region.text: the land west of the 1922 outline, around Chefchaouen and Oued Laou

ledger.note: 1924: Spain pulls back from Chefchaouen and Oued Laou. Primo de Rivera visited Ben Taieb in late July 1924 and changed the withdrawal plans, pulling back from Chefchaouen and Oued Laou to the 'Primo Line'; the western growth of Cliopatria's 1924 shape is read as this land. The page gives no day and does not say who occupied it.

region.text: the frontier of French Morocco that the Rifians attacked in April 1925

ledger.note: 1925: the Rifians attack the French line on 12 April. 'On 12 April 1925, in an event known as the battle of Oureghla' the Rifians attacked; Abd el-Krim 'advanced south into French Morocco, defeating French forces' and threatened Fes (Republic of the Rif page).

region.text: Alhucemas Bay and Ajdir, the Rif coast and capital (secured by the Spanish fleet and army in September 1925)

ledger.note: 1925: Spain secures Alhucemas Bay in September. The Spanish fleet and army secured Alhucemas Bay in September 1925 (the page gives no day); the bay and Ajdir, the Rif coast and capital, are read as lost to Spain.

region.text: the frontier of French Morocco that the Rifians attacked in April 1925

ledger.note: 1926: Abd el-Krim surrenders on 27 May. 'Abd el-Krim... surrendered to French authorities on May 27, 1926' (the Republic page: to Petain on 26 May).

region.text: the front with the Spanish zone, 1921-1926

ledger.note: 1926: the Rif front closes with the surrender of 27 May 1926.

minus.text: Alhucemas Bay and Ajdir, the Rif coast and capital (secured by the Spanish fleet and army in September 1925)

ledger.note: 1926: the Republic of the Rif ends on 27 May. It 'was dissolved by Spanish and French occupation forces on 27 May 1926'; the Spanish protectorate in Morocco is the successor.

wars.name: Rif War

zones.text: the Rif and the frontier of the French zone

wars.outcome: Spanish-French victory and the Spanish conquest of the Rif; Abd el-Krim surrendered on 27 May 1926 (infobox: war ended June 1926).
wars.note: Infobox 17 May 1921 to June 1926; Annual 1 July 1921; France joined Spain from 1924; Oureghla 12 April 1925; Alhucemas landing September 1925. The last pocket of resistance (Akhmas) was occupied on 9 July 1927.

certainty.note: The Rif's frontiers were the lines of a war and of tribal allegiance; the page gives no boundaries or area.

sources.title: Republic of the Rif
sources.note: 18 September 1921 proclamation, 1923 constitution, April 1925 advance, dissolution 27 May 1926, capital Ajdir.

sources.title: Rif War
sources.note: Annual 1 July 1921, the 1924 Spanish withdrawal to the Primo Line, Oureghla 12 April 1925, Alhucemas September 1925, surrender 27 May 1926.

notes: Cliopatria draws the republic as two small shapes (1922-1923 and 1924-1925) though the state was proclaimed on 18 September 1921 and ended on 27 May 1926, so new keyframes were added for 1921 and 1926. The pages give no boundary or area, so the outlines are Cliopatria's; the 1925 gains in the French zone (Ouergha valley) are not drawn as land held because the pages say only that the Rifians 'advanced south into French Morocco' and fought at Oureghla (a contest band is used instead). The republic's later seat (after Ajdir fell) is not on the pages opened. The Rif Republic page does not mention the Tangier zone. Counterparts: kingdom-of-spain (eu group; the Spanish protectorate in Morocco is not a separate Cliopatria row) and french-africa (af-08).
